newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch assert EU credentials at transport meeting.
newsitem.headline: Dutch assert EU credentials at transport meeting.

text.p: The Netherlands chaired its first informal ministerial meeting as European Union president on Friday, asserting its EU credentials by unveiling new car plates and road signs, each with a European flavour.
Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma told reporters that she hoped the plates and signs would serve as a model for the bloc's 15 members.
The road signs are to be put up on three highways out of Amsterdam, giving the distance, in kilometres, to a number of European capitals.
"By unveiling this, I want to give the European road sign system a push," Jorritsma said.
The new Dutch car plate, which incorporates the EU's 12-star motif, comes into use in 1998, although Jorritsma acknowledged that registration plates may by then be a relic of the past.
"It is highly possible that, as technology advances, the number plate will gradually disappear and be replaced by an electronic system of vehicle registration," she said.
Ministers earlier discussed how to coordinate road toll systems, with the Dutch hosts proposing to introduce an electric road toll system in its larger cities by 2001.
"This is partly why we're so keen to introduce inter-operability of (road toll) systems," Jorritsma said.
Later on Friday, ministers will tackle the thorny issue of transit rights through Switzerland, hoping to agree a common front for talks with the Swiss, but Jorritsma warned against dramatic advances.
"Don't expect any spectacular announcement. We're not even talking to the Swiss," she said.

Outside the meeting, protestors calling theselves "Platform to Another Europe", complained about EU pressure on the Swiss and erected a 10-metre high inflatable mountain, representing the threatened Swiss Alps.
Switzerland wants to sharply reduce the amount of freight traffic on its roads, favouring a switch to rail.
The informal meeting concludes on Saturday with talks on air traffic management.
